findings.text: Estimated utilization uses a sticky unchanged marker to coordinate PELT refresh with deferred consolidation. The change hook clears the marker when averages move, and consolidation later re-arms it after deciding among adoption, smoothing, or retention under feature gating, increase adoption, decrease smoothing with closeness and full-service guards, and tracing.

Two load-average refresh operations report whether decay changed entity state. One serves entities associated with a runqueue using membership, runnable, and currency inputs and additionally refreshes derived averages, notifies estimate tracking, and traces; the other serves blocked entities with neutral inputs and similarly refreshes and traces.

Runnable contribution of an entity is absent when delayed. Otherwise task entities reflect queued presence while group entities reflect stored runnable weight in hierarchical builds, collapsing to queued presence alone in simpler builds.

Per-queue PELT time compensates for throttled intervals in bandwidth-controlled builds by removing accumulated throttled duration from either a frozen throttled clock or the underlying runqueue clock, while simpler builds expose the underlying clock directly. A separate predicate reports throttling only when bandwidth control is active and the queue flag is set, otherwise constantly negative.

Leaf queue membership maintains bottom-up ordering so descendants precede ancestors, using a membership flag against duplicates and a temporary branch anchor for disconnected subtrees. Roots append at the tail, children of enlisted parents insert beside the parent, and orphaned children extend the pending branch until connection or tree top resets the anchor, with a debug check asserting full connection after propagation.

Hierarchical builds walk the full ancestor chain with leaf bookkeeping and ancestor refresh, while minimal builds walk a single entity, treat leaf insertion as trivially successful, disable the connection assertion, and reduce propagation to a no-op.

Runqueue acquisition disables interrupts then takes either a shared core word or a private queue word chosen by core-scheduling state, with nesting level support. The nested path disables preemption, uses the private word when core scheduling is globally off, and otherwise samples the selector, locks the indicated word, validates stability, and drops the preemption guard without rescheduling on success.

Pinning a held runqueue records lock state, restricts clock flags to skip requests, clears per-acquisition update state, and asserts absence of unexpected balance callbacks apart from a tolerated push entry. Release is unpin then interrupt-enabled unlock; unpin promotes large flag values to an updated mark and invalidates extensible-scheduler clock caching, while repin restores lock state and merges stashed clock flags.
Task group migration, eager rescheduling, queue preemption checks, and deferred balance processing are exported runqueue operations shared across scheduling files.
Load-average refresh for associated and blocked entities plus fair-queue attachment aging are exported load-tracking helpers shared between fair scheduling and PELT accounting.
Autogroup eligibility and exit handling plus extensible-scheduler cgroup migration are exported group-membership operations.

Group migration serializes against runqueue locking, resolves cgroup then autogroup identity, optionally notifies the extensible scheduler for non-autogroup moves, and defers the wakeup effect until after the guarded region as either rescheduling a running task or checking preemption for a queued task, followed by draining balance callbacks.

Automatic grouping applies only to root-group members whose threads are not exiting. Exit handling forces a group refresh before notification paths invalidate shared signal references, and group selection prefers the signal autogroup when a runtime toggle is enabled and eligibility holds, otherwise preserving the supplied group or unconditionally preserving it in builds without the feature.

Rescheduling requests funnel through an eager wrapper into a flag-parameterized core requiring the runqueue lock. It promotes lazy requests for idle tasks, suppresses duplicates when need is already pending, and otherwise sets the thread flag locally with a preemption mark or remotely through polling-aware delivery that signals only non-polling targets.

Atomic flag setting either merges a bit with a compare-exchange retry loop and reports whether polling was clear, or unconditionally sets the thread flag and reports success. Remote rescheduling relies on the first form to avoid unnecessary signaling.

Queue preemption dispatches to the queued task class on match with the next class, otherwise dispatches to the next class and additionally forces rescheduling and advances that class only when the newcomer ranks above it under pointer ordering. A clock-update skip is requested when the donor remains queued while the current task already needs rescheduling.

Deferred runqueue callbacks are spliced as a linked list under the runqueue lock, drained by unlinking each entry before invocation, and executed outside the pinned region through an unpin, drain, and repin cycle when pin state exists. A split splice preserves a distinguished push entry on the queue to avoid an observable empty list across lock sections.

Observed entity state includes a delayed marker, queue membership, runnable weight, parent linkage, depth, assigned fair queue, and an averaging block with estimate plus unchanged marker, utilization and runnable averages, and last-update timestamp with a narrow-counter copy.

Observed runqueue state includes current and donor tasks, next class pointer, leaf list with membership flags and branch anchor, callback head, clock-update flags, throttled PELT accounting, and core-scheduling enablement selecting shared versus private locking. Observed fair-queue state includes task-group linkage, throttle flags, and averaging timestamps.

Cross-queue attachment optionally ages load by decaying the entity to the source timestamp and re-stamping it with the destination timestamp when enabled and when prior timestamp plus source queue exist. Timestamp reads are direct on wide-counter builds and copy-validated retries on narrow-counter builds.

Task-to-queue linkage either rewrites fair parent, depth, and queue pointers plus real-time queue and parent with root fallback when group scheduling is inactive, or does nothing in minimal builds. Group lookup returns either the assigned group or null by configuration, and fair-group online handling can be a no-op.

Extensible-scheduler cgroup migration pairs preparation with completion by clearing the stored source on every call while notifying only when a source exists, a scheduler is bound under cgroup-mutex protection, and the operation bit is set. Group-to-cgroup mapping treats missing groups and cgroup-less autogroups as the default root, with a no-op migration entry in minimal builds.

Torn timestamp reads on narrow-counter builds, lost wakeups from polling-aware remote signaling, stale PELT time under throttling, misordered leaf traversal from incorrect splicing, and premature empty observation from mishandled push-callback splicing each risk fairness, accounting, or liveness faults if guards or ordering weaken.

Holding runqueue state across pin transitions without the prescribed unpin, drain, and repin cycle, or acquiring the wrong shared versus private lock word, risks lock imbalance, missed clock updates, and corrupted deferred-callback execution.
